title: He Sold the Eiffel Tower. Twice. #shorts
description:
In 1925, con man Victor Lustig posed as a French government official and invited scrap-metal dealers to a secret meeting. He told them the Eiffel Tower was too expensive to maintain and would be sold for scrap. One dealer, André Poisson, paid about $70,000 in total, according to Smithsonian Magazine. Poisson was too embarrassed to go to the police, so Lustig came back and tried a second sale. Then he fled to the US. A true story.

Question: would you have fallen for it? Tell me in the comments.

Made with AI assistance (research, voice and artwork). Events are simplified for storytelling.
